content.title: Scan a Passport Photo for Visa Application on iPhone
content.meta_description: Crop and scan passport or visa photos to exact 2x2 inch or 35x45 mm dimensions on iPhone. Use a face guide, then export for online applications or printing.
content.h1: How to Scan a Passport Photo for Your Application on iPhone
content.quick_answer: To scan a passport photo on your iPhone, use an app with a dedicated ID photo mode. This mode helps you capture a photo with a face-position guide and crop it to specific sizes like 2x2 inches or 35x45 mm. You can then export the photo as a digital image file or a printable sheet, ensuring it meets application requirements.
intro: Applying for a visa or renewing a passport often requires a digital photo that meets strict size and proportion guidelines. You need to frame your face correctly and crop the image to specific dimensions like 2x2 inches or 35x45 mm.
This guide shows you how to use Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit on your iPhone or iPad to create compliant passport and visa photos. You can capture, crop, and export photos accurately from home.
Remember to always check the most current and specific photo requirements with the official issuing authority for your passport or visa.
content.steps_heading: Scan Your Passport Photo with Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit

steps.title: Open the App and Choose ID Photo Mode
steps.detail: Launch Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit. Select the 'ID photo mode' from the main screen. This mode activates specific tools for passport and visa photos.

steps.title: Capture Your Photo Using the Guide
steps.detail: Position yourself or the subject in front of the camera. The app displays a face-position guide on screen. Align the face within this guide to ensure correct head size and placement for standard passport and visa requirements. Take the photo.

steps.title: Select Photo Size and Review Crop
steps.detail: After capturing, the app will let you choose common passport and visa sizes, such as 2x2 inches or 35x45 mm. Review the automatic crop and make any minor adjustments to ensure the photo meets your specific application's requirements for head size and margin.

steps.title: Export Your Digital Image or Print Sheet
steps.detail: Once cropped, you can export the photo. Choose to save a single digital image file, which is often required for online applications. Alternatively, you can export a print sheet with multiple copies of the photo, ready for printing.

content.alternatives_heading: Other Ways to Get a Passport Photo

alternatives.method: Using the iOS Camera and Photos app
alternatives.how: You can take a photo with your iPhone's Camera app. Then, use the Photos app to manually crop it. Live Text can copy text from photos but does not help with photo formatting.
alternatives.best_for: Informal photos not requiring precise size or alignment.
alternatives.limitation: The Photos app lacks specific passport photo cropping dimensions and a face-position guide. You must manually measure and guess proportions for head size and placement.

alternatives.how: Many websites offer free tools to crop photos to passport dimensions. You upload your image, and the site processes it.
alternatives.best_for: Quick, one-off adjustments if you already have a photo.
alternatives.limitation: These tools require uploading your sensitive identity photo to a third-party server. Free versions may also have limits on file size or daily usage. Always confirm their privacy policy before use.

alternatives.how: Visit a photo studio that specializes in passport and visa photos. They have professional equipment and knowledge of various country requirements.
alternatives.best_for: High likelihood of compliance and convenience, especially for complex requirements.
alternatives.limitation: This option incurs a cost and requires a visit to a physical location, which may not be convenient.

All photo processing, including cropping and sizing, runs on your iPhone. Your sensitive identity photos are not uploaded to any server, keeping them private.

content.tips_heading: Tips for a Compliant Passport Photo
tips: Always confirm the specific photo requirements (size, background, head position, expression) with the official government authority or visa issuing body before you take and submit your photo. Requirements change often.
Ensure even lighting on your face with no harsh shadows or glare. A plain, light-colored background (white or off-white) is usually required. Avoid complex patterns or textures behind you.
Maintain a neutral facial expression with both eyes open. Do not wear hats, scarves, or other head coverings unless for religious purposes, and ensure your full face is visible.
Many online passport and visa applications ask for a digital photo upload with a pixel-size and file-size range. Verify these digital specifications in addition to physical dimensions.

For general document scanning using your iPhone without an app, consider the built-in Notes or Files apps. For scanning business cards into contacts, refer to our guide on scanning business cards to contacts.

faqs.question: How do you format a photo to 2x2 inches (US) or 35x45 mm (UK/Schengen/India)?
faqs.answer: Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit's 'ID photo mode' crops a photo to common passport and visa sizes. You can select standard sizes like 2x2 inches (51x51 mm) for the United States, or 35x45 mm for the United Kingdom, Schengen countries, and India.

faqs.question: How does the on-screen face-position guide help align head proportions?
faqs.answer: The app's face-position guide appears in the camera view within 'ID photo mode'. It helps you align your face correctly within the frame, ensuring your head is centered and occupies the right proportion of the photo, as required by official guidelines.

faqs.question: Can you export both a digital image file and a printable photo sheet?
faqs.answer: Yes, after cropping your photo in 'ID photo mode', you can export it in two ways. You can save it as a single digital image file for online applications, or as a print sheet containing multiple copies of your photo, ready for printing at home or a photo service.

faqs.question: Why must you verify specific photo requirements with the official government authority?
faqs.answer: Passport and visa photo requirements, including background color, head size, and recency, differ by country and can change. Always confirm the latest official requirements directly with the issuing authority's official site to avoid application delays or rejections.

faqs.question: Are your identity photos processed privately on the iPhone?
faqs.answer: Yes, all processing, including scanning, filters, and text recognition (OCR), runs directly on your iPhone. Your identity photos are stored locally on your device unless you choose to save them to a cloud service yourself.

problems: "Review the automatic crop and make any minor adjustments to ensure the photo meets your specific application's requirements for head size and margin." (in steps, step 3, detail) - The app facts for 'id_photo' do not state that users can "make any minor adjustments" to the crop. It only says it "Crops a photo to common passport and visa sizes".

"Ensure a clean, well-defined capture for your photo with automatic edge detection, which crops and straightens the image as you shoot." (in feature_points, feature_id: auto_edge, benefit) - The 'auto_edge' feature is described for "page borders" and "the page". Applying it to a "photo" (specifically a passport photo) is a misapplication of the feature's description. The 'id_photo' feature already covers cropping for passport photos.
